solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drive off with yours truly (today's compiler), bowled over after getting a prize

indicators.note: the reversed chunk comes after the single letter the clue says is got, so that letter leads
something bowled over is knocked flat and turned head over heels, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: DR is the usual abbreviation for drive, as in a street name
off means away, as in 'he's off today'
yours truly is the speaker referring to themself, ME
the setter of this puzzle signs as Dac

explanation.surface: A setter is chauffeured away, overcome with emotion after winning a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled over' turns the whole string round, giving CADEMYAWARD. Setters often put their own pseudonym in a clue as 'today's compiler'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar, given by the film Academy, is a celebrated prize for screen work.

clue.text: Beastly film concluded with O Reed and I appearing drunk

indicators.note: drunk means staggering about, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild night with actor Oliver Reed ends with the speaker drunk too.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Reed was a hard-drinking English actor, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1986 Australian comedy is named after its crocodile-hunting hero, so it is a film full of beasts.

clue.text: Division in party as Republican confronts Democrat

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

explanation.surface: A political party splits when a Republican squares up to a Democrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife and disagreement within a group is a division of opinion.

clue.text: Account of me getting stuck in sea near St Malo?

indicators.note: one piece is wedged inside another, as a thing stuck in something

parts.note: St Malo is a French port, and the French for sea is mer
moi is French for me, suggested by the French setting

explanation.surface: Someone recounts being stranded in the waters off the Breton coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the sea must be named in French, as at St Malo in Brittany.
explanation.definitionFit: A written personal recollection of one's life is an account of it.

clue.text: Money dating back to 18th century: ill-gotten gains, in a way

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are placed inside the other two pieces

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way

indicators.note: ill here means badly, so the letters are got into a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Old currency is linked with dishonestly acquired profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-gotten' reworks the letters of 'gains' into SIGNA, and 'in' places that inside the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This paper currency was issued in revolutionary France in the 1790s.

clue.text: Support male taken into nick?

indicators.note: one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to arrest

explanation.surface: A man is hauled into the police station, perhaps for support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang both for a police station and for arresting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair's arm rest is a support for the elbow.

clue.text: White van man might fulfil promise

definitions.meaning: a white van man is a British stereotype of a delivery driver, who carries parcels to the door
to fulfil a promise is to come up with what was expected

explanation.walkthrough: 'White van man' is a British label for a brash van driver, typically a courier or tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do what was promised, and a courier literally brings the parcels.

clue.text: Light-hearted film from previous series

indicators.note: the letters come as a consecutive series within the words, read straight through

explanation.surface: A comedy movie appears to come from an earlier run of programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'series' is an unusual signal: the answer is a continuous run of letters in 'from previous'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boisterous comic film or play is called by this name in reviews.

clue.text: Sanctions examples of Churchill's rhetoric?

definitions.meaning: sanctions here is a verb, meaning authorises
Churchill's wartime speeches could be called ...

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into WAR and RANTS, a joke on Churchill's wartime oratory.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise or justify an action is to give it official sanction.

clue.text: Animal round front of parlour: unusually big problem

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a label on extra-large clothes
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A creature circling the front room is a real headache.
explanation.definitionFit: The American marsupial is a well-known animal.

clue.text: Trouble a doctor's encountered, going round African country

indicators.note: going round means turning back the other way, so the string is reversed

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
MO, medical officer, is a doctor, and the apostrophe S adds the letter S

explanation.surface: A doctor makes rounds and meets illness in an African land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns the whole string back to front, giving SOMALIA; 'encountered' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This nation lies on the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Suggesting petty officer's wrong to appear in TV show

indicators.note: the pieces turn up inside the other piece

parts.note: a prog is short for a programme
PO is the abbreviation for petty officer; the possessive adds no letter
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A naval rating's misdeed is suggested as material for a television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting an idea forward is proposing it, i.e. suggesting it.

clue.text: Young swimmer injured in revel

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so these letters are knocked out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: A youthful bather gets hurt during some partying.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a young eel, which swims upriver from the sea.

clue.text: Keep quiet, attending this daily noisy gathering?

parts.note: SH is the request for silence
The Independent newspaper, where the puzzle appears, is nicknamed the Indy

explanation.surface: A reader is told to hush while going to a newspaper's lively event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attending' just joins the pieces. 'This daily' is the newspaper printing the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal word for a noisy disturbance or rowdy party.

clue.text: Extra duty making Pasteur terribly cross

indicators.note: terribly suggests going badly wrong, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: An extra levy enrages the French scientist Louis Pasteur.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra levy charged on high incomes is an additional tax, a duty on top.

clue.text: Tough jailbird shown round a prison

indicators.note: the outer piece is shown wrapped around the rest

parts.note: a con is a convict
stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A hardened inmate is given a tour of a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbreakable, like the metal, is tough and firm.

clue.text: I'm surprised business graduate has settled within Italian region

indicators.note: one piece has come to rest inside another

parts.note: lordy is an exclamation of surprise
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a business graduate has moved to northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: This region of northern Italy has Milan as its capital.

clue.text: Where reporters are showing urge to fight

parts.note: to press is to urge
to box is to fight

explanation.surface: Journalists gather where there is a strong urge to scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists sit in a press box at a stadium to cover the game.

clue.text: Garment supported by Truro consumer?

parts.note: Truro, in Cornwall, is in the South-West of England, SW
an eater is a consumer of food

explanation.surface: Clothing is endorsed by a shopper from Truro.
explanation.walkthrough: Truro is the county town of Cornwall, at England's south-western tip. 'supported by' is a link: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted top or jumper is a garment.

clue.text: S America imports tea, for example

indicators.note: imports means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: US is America
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: South America brings in tea, among other goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce an instance, like 'like' does.

clue.text: Instrument pipe-shaped, and mostly easy to stretch

parts.note: a U-bend is a pipe shaped like the letter U

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: tensile means able to be stretched

explanation.surface: A tool is tube-shaped and fairly flexible.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool or implement, especially in a kitchen, is an instrument.

clue.text: Hand holding sovereign and gold coin of old

indicators.note: holding means one piece clasps the others inside it

parts.note: fin is slang for a hand
a sovereign is a pound coin, and L is the abbreviation for pound
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A hand clutches a sovereign and some gold, old money.
explanation.walkthrough: The FLORIN was a British two-shilling coin, withdrawn after decimal currency arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a two-shilling piece in old British money.

clue.text: Provoke complaint after heading off

indicators.note: the heading is the opening letter, and it comes off

parts.note: a grouse is a grumble or complaint

explanation.surface: Lodging a grievance once leaving is bound to stir trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or excite someone is to provoke them.

clue.text: Bird wailed quite regularly when bitten by dog

indicators.note: bitten by means held in the dog's jaws, so the letters go inside it

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of dog

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A bird cries out steadily as a dog bites it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'wailed', and 'when bitten by' puts them in the dog's jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald eagle is the national bird of the USA.

clue.text: Old-time flat

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for ..., a time of day

explanation.definitionFit: Poets once used the word for evening, and a level surface is flat.

clue.text: Accounts expert, one hears

definitions.meaning: a person who inspects a company's books
a listener, from the Latin audire, to hear

explanation.definitionFit: A checker of financial books, and literally a listener.

clue.text: Starter in restaurant is fish, pan-fried dish

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A restaurant's first course is fish cooked in a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A patty of minced meat or fish, fried in a pan, is this dish.

clue.text: He's in gallery, constructed in old architectural style

indicators.note: constructed means built up from parts, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A man is in a gallery that was built in an old style.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'He's' is a letter here, since it stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the first Gothic style of English cathedrals, from about 1180 to 1250.
